title: Z80 SIO channel registers
covers: the read and write registers of each channel of the Zilog Z80 SIO: status, special receive condition, interrupt vector and the control registers WR0 to WR7

rows.text: WR6 stores the byte written to it: the transmit sync character in Monosync mode, the first eight bits of the Bisync sync character, or an External Sync transmit sync character.
In SDLC mode WR6 stores the byte written to it as the secondary address field, compared with the address field of the SDLC frame.
WR6 bits D7 to D0 are Sync 7 to Sync 0.
WR7 stores the byte written to it: the receive sync character in Monosync mode, the last eight bits of the Bisync sync character, or the SDLC flag character 0111 1110.
WR7 is not used in the External Sync mode.
WR7 bits D7 to D0 are Sync 15 to Sync 8; the capture's header line drops the D0 label.
For SDLC, WR7 must be programmed to 0111 1110 for flag recognition.
WR5 contains control bits for the transmitter, except D2, which affects the transmitter and receiver.
WR5 stores D0, Transmit CRC Enable; set as a character is loaded into the transmit shift register, it makes CRC be calculated on that character.
When the RTS bit is set, the RTS pin goes Low.
In asynchronous mode, when the RTS bit is reset, RTS goes High only after all the bits of the character are transmitted and the transmit buffer is empty.
In synchronous modes the RTS pin directly follows the state of the RTS bit.
WR5 stores D2, which selects the CRC-16 polynomial when set and the SDLC polynomial when reset, for both transmitter and receiver.
Data is not transmitted until the Transmit Enable bit D3 is set, and the Transmit Data output is held marking.
Send Break D4, when set, immediately forces the Transmit Data output to the spacing condition; when reset, TxD returns to marking.
WR5 D6 and D5 select the bits per character: 00 five or less, 01 seven, 10 six, 11 eight.
DTR D7, when set, makes the DTR pin active (Low); when reset, inactive (High).
The CPU formats a character of five bits or fewer right-justified, least-significant bit first, as Table 28 shows.
CRC is not sent automatically unless the Transmit CRC Enable bit is set when the Transmit Underrun condition occurs.
With SDLC mode selected, the CRC generator and checker are preset to 1s and the SDLC polynomial must be selected; otherwise both polynomials preset to 0s.
Data or sync characters being transmitted are completely sent if Transmit Enable is reset; if disabled during CRC transmission, sync or flag characters are sent instead.
MAME clears the pending transmit interrupt when WR5 is written with the Transmit Enable bit D3 clear.
MAME forces TxD to 0 at once while D4 is set; once it is clear it drives TxD to the transmitter's current level m_txd, not to a fixed marking level.
WR3 contains receiver logic control bits and parameters.
WR3 stores D0, Receiver Enable; a 1 programmed into it allows receive operations to begin.
Receiver Enable should be set only after all other receive parameters are set and the receiver is completely initialized.
WR3 stores D1, Sync Character Load Inhibit; if selected, the leading sync characters are kept out of the receive buffers.
CRC calculation is not stopped by sync character stripping, so this feature should be enabled only at the beginning of the message.
WR3 stores D2, Address Search Mode: in SDLC mode, messages matching neither WR6 nor 1111 1111 are rejected, with no receive interrupts.
WR3 stores D3, Receiver CRC Enable; set, it starts or restarts CRC calculation at the last character moved from the receive shift register to the buffer stack.
The Z80 SIO enters the Hunt phase automatically after a reset.
The Hunt phase is re-entered by writing a 1 to D4, which sets the Sync/Hunt bit D4 in RR0.
MAME enters hunt mode on a D4 write only if WR4 selects a synchronous mode, while row 9 states the D4 write with no such condition.
If Auto Enables D5 is set, DCD and CTS become the receiver and transmitter enables; if not, they are only inputs to their RR0 status bits.
WR3 D7 and D6 select the receive bits per character: 00 five, 01 seven, 10 six, 11 eight.
Both bits D7 and D6 may be changed while a character is being assembled, but before the programmed number of bits is reached.

rows.text: WR4 contains control bits that affect both the receiver and the transmitter.
In the initialization routine WR4 should be set before WR1, WR3, WR5, WR6 and WR7.
WR4 stores D0, Parity Enable; if set, a parity bit position is added to transmitted data and expected in received data.
In receive mode the parity bit received is transferred to the CPU as part of the character, unless eight bits per character is selected.
WR4 stores D1, Parity Even/Odd: if parity is specified, it decides whether the parity bit is sent and checked as even or odd, 1 being even.
WR4 stores D3 and D2, the stop bits per asynchronous character: 01 one, 10 one and a half, 11 two; 00 selects a synchronous mode.
The receiver always checks for one stop bit.
WR4 stores D5 and D4, the sync mode: 00 8-bit programmed sync, 01 16-bit programmed sync, 10 SDLC mode, 11 External Sync mode.
WR4 D7 and D6 select the multiplier between the clock and the data rate: 00 x1, 01 x16, 10 x32, 11 x64.
Synchronous modes need the x1 clock rate; asynchronous modes may use any rate, but the same for receiver and transmitter.
The system clock must be at least 4.5 times the data rate; with x1, bit synchronization must be performed externally.
WR2 is the interrupt vector register and occurs in Channel B only.
MAME stores a WR2 write on channel A as it does on channel B, and logs the INT/DMA mode bits for channel A.
V7 to V4 and V0 are always returned exactly as written; V3 to V1 are returned as written if Status Affects Vector is 0, otherwise modified.
WR2 bits D7 to D0 are V7 to V0.
WR1 contains the control bits for the various interrupt and Wait/Ready modes.
WR1 stores D0, External/Status Interrupt Enable, which allows interrupts from DCD, CTS or SYNC transitions, Break/Abort detection and termination, or the Tx Underrun/EOM latch setting.
WR1 stores D1, Transmitter Interrupt Enable; if set, interrupts occur whenever the transmitter buffer becomes empty.
WR1 stores D2, Status Affects Vector, Channel B only: if clear the fixed WR2 vector is returned on interrupt acknowledge, if set a variable one.
With Status Affects Vector, V3 V2 V1 give 000 Ch B transmit buffer empty up to 111 Ch A special receive condition, as Table 16 lists.
WR1 stores D4 and D3, the receive interrupt mode: 00 disabled, 01 on first character only, 10 all characters with parity special, 11 all without.
WR1 stores D7, Wait/Ready Enable; the Wait/Ready function is enabled by setting it to 1.
The text says the Ready function is selected by setting D5 to 1, while later text makes D5 the Wait/Ready on Receive/Transmit bit.
If D5, Wait/Ready on Receive/Transmit, is 1 the Wait/Ready function follows the receive buffer; if 0, the transmit buffer.
Wait and Ready can be used in Transmit or Receive modes, but not both at once.
Table 18 gives the Wait/Ready output states for each combination of modes.
The Ready function can occur with the Z80 SIO not selected; READY becomes inactive when IORQ and CS become active, so the DMA controller is not enabled then.
The Wait function is active only when the CPU reads data not yet received, or, under program control, writes while the transmit buffer is full.
The Wait function is selected by setting D6 to 0.
In the Wait function the WAIT/READY output is open drain and goes Low when active.
Each channel has eight write registers, WR7 to WR0, that the system program programs separately to configure the channel.
Programming a write register other than WR0 takes two bytes; the first, stored in WR0, has three pointer bits D2-D0 selecting the register.
After pointing to a register, a programmer can read to test a read register or write to initialize a write register.
WR0 is unique because all the basic commands can be given with a single byte, and reset initializes the pointer bits to WR0.
The basic commands and CRC controls are in the first byte of any write register access, and these registers are addressed as commands, not data.
WR0 is the command register, and it also carries the CRC reset codes and points to the other registers.
WR0 stores D2-D0, the pointer bits that determine which write register the next byte writes to, or which read register it reads from.
The first byte written to each channel after a reset, by Reset command or reset input, goes to WR0.
MAME stores the whole command byte in WR0 before a Channel Reset command runs, and its channel reset never clears WR0, so pointer bits in D2-D0 stay selected.
Following a read or write to any register except WR0, the pointer points to WR0.
Bits D5-D3 are encoded to issue the seven basic Z80 SIO commands listed in Table 13.
CRC Reset Codes 0 and 1, WR0 D7 and D6, used together select one of three reset commands, listed in Table 14.
WR0 D7 D6 = 01 resets the Receive CRC checker, which is initialized to 1s for the SDLC mode.
WR0 D7 D6 = 10 resets the Transmit CRC generator, normally to 0s and to 1s in SDLC mode.
WR0 D7 D6 = 11 resets the Tx Underrun/End of Message latch.
MAME resets the Tx Underrun/EOM latch (RR0_TX_UNDERRUN) only when m_tx_in_pkt is set; otherwise the command is logged as not accepted.
WR0 D7 D6 = 00 is the null code, with no effect.
The second byte is the control word written into the selected register to configure the Z80 SIO.
On the Reset Receive CRC Checker command MAME also clears its receive CRC enable flag, m_rx_crc_en.
RR0 contains the status of the receive and transmit buffers, the DCD, CTS and SYNC inputs, the Transmit Underrun/EOM latch and the Break/Abort latch.
Receive Character Available D0 is reset when the receive FIFO is empty.
Receive Character Available D0 is set when at least one character is available in the receive buffer.
Any interrupting condition sets Interrupt Pending D1, readable only in Channel A; it is reset when all the interrupting conditions are satisfied.
Interrupt Pending D1 is always 0 in Channel B.
Transmit Buffer Empty D2 is set whenever the transmit buffer becomes empty, and reset when a character is loaded into the transmit buffer.
Transmit Buffer Empty D2 is not set while a CRC character is being sent in a synchronous or SDLC mode.
Transmit Buffer Empty D2 is in the set condition after a reset.
DCD D3 shows the state of the DCD input at the time of the last change of any of the five External/Status bits.
Any transition of the DCD input latches the DCD bit and causes an External/Status interrupt.
To read the current state of DCD, read it immediately following a Reset External/Status Interrupt command.
Sync/Hunt D4 is controlled differently in the asynchronous, synchronous and SDLC modes.
In asynchronous modes D4 shows the SYNC input: High-to-Low sets it and causes an External/Status interrupt (if enabled); Low-to-High clears it and sets the interrupt.
When the External/Status interrupt comes from any other input or condition, D4 shows the inverted state of the SYNC pin at the time of the change.
To read the current state of the SYNC input, D4 must be read immediately following a Reset External/Status Interrupt command.
In External Sync mode D4 works as in asynchronous mode, except Enter Hunt Mode enables the external sync detection logic.
In External Sync mode SYNC is held High until synchronization is achieved, then driven Low on the second RxC rising edge after the last sync bit.
In External Sync mode SYNC is kept Low until the CPU reports lost synchronization; its High-to-Low transition sets D4 and the External/Status interrupt.
When SYNC goes High again another External/Status interrupt is generated, and Enter Hunt Mode is set whenever synchronization is lost or the message ends.
In Monosync and Bisync receive modes D4 is first set by Enter Hunt Mode, and reset, with an External/Status interrupt, when character synchronization is established.
The CPU clears that interrupt with Reset External/Status Interrupt, and sets Enter Hunt Mode on end of message or lost synchronization, which sets D4 and an interrupt.
In Monosync and Bisync modes the SYNC pin is an output that goes Low when a sync pattern is detected.
In SDLC mode D4 is first set by Enter Hunt Mode or by disabling the receiver, and reset to 0 when the opening flag of the first frame is detected.
In SDLC mode an External/Status interrupt is also generated on that reset, and D4 can be set again only by Enter Hunt Mode or by disabling the receiver.
CTS D5 is similar to DCD, but shows the inverted state of the CTS pin.
Transmit Underrun/End of Message D6 is set following a reset, internal or external.
Only the Reset Transmit Underrun/EOM Latch command can reset D6.
MAME clears D6 with that command only while a packet is being transmitted; otherwise it logs that the command is not accepted.
When the transmit underrun condition occurs D6 is set, causing the External/Status interrupt that Reset External/Status Interrupt resets.
MAME also sets D6 when the transmitter is disabled, and a comment says it is not sure real hardware does.
In asynchronous receive mode Break/Abort D7 is set when a Break sequence, a null character plus a framing error, is detected; the External/Status interrupt is set if enabled.
The interrupt service routine must issue Reset External/Status Interrupt so that the termination of the Break can be recognized.
D7 is reset when the termination of the Break sequence is detected, which also sets the External/Status interrupt.
Reset External/Status Interrupt must then be issued to look for the next Break, and a single extraneous null character after the break should be read and discarded.
In SDLC receive mode D7 is set by detection of an Abort sequence of seven or more 1s.
In SDLC mode the External/Status interrupt for an Abort is handled the same way as for a Break, and D7 is not used in synchronous receive mode.
RR2 to RR0 are read for status; to read a register other than the captured 'RRD' the pointer byte is first written to WR0, then an input instruction reads it.
The status bits of RR0 and RR1 are grouped so that, for a Special Receive Condition interrupt, all the error bits can be read from RR1.
MAME latches DCD when an external change is triggered, but sets the DCD bit when the input level m_dcd is 0, the same inversion as CTS.

rows.text: Reading RR1 returns the Special Receive condition status bits and the residue codes for the I-field in the SDLC receive mode.
All Sent D0 is set in asynchronous modes when all the characters have completely cleared the transmitter; its transitions cause no interrupts and it is always set in synchronous modes.
In SDLC receive mode Residue Codes D3-D1 give the I-field length when it is not a whole number of characters, meaningful only when End-of-Frame is set.
For eight bits per character, residue codes 100, 010, 110, 001, 101 give 0 I-field bits in the previous byte and 3 to 7 in the second previous byte.
I-field bits are always right justified.
For another receive character length a similar table may be built; with no residue the codes 011, 111 and 000 give 8 bits.
Table 34 gives the no-residue codes by receive character length: 8 bits 011, 7 bits 000, 6 bits 010, 5 bits 001.
When parity is enabled, Parity Error D4 is set for characters whose parity does not match the programmed sense, and stays set until the Error Reset command.
Receive Overrun Error D5 means more than three characters were received without a CPU read; it is latched until Error Reset.
CRC/Framing Error D6 is set for a character with a framing error, not latched; in synchronous and SDLC modes it gives the CRC check result.
End-of-Frame D7, SDLC only, shows a valid ending flag was received; it is reset by Error Reset and updated by the first character of the next frame.

rows.text: RR2 contains the interrupt vector written into WR2 if the Status Affects Vector control bit is not set.
If Status Affects Vector is set, RR2 contains the modified vector, modified by the highest priority interrupting condition at the time of the read.
If no interrupts are pending, the vector is modified with V3 = 0, V2 = 1 and V1 = 1.
RR2 is read only through Channel B.
MAME returns the vector when RR2 is read through channel B, and returns 0 instead of a vector when it is read through channel A.
RR2 bits D7 to D0 are V7 to V0, with V3, V2 and V1 variable if Status Affects Vector is programmed.
